pr_title: changefeedccl: Correct check that job ID argument is an integer
pr_body:
Correctly check job ID is an integer.

Fixes #108500

Release note: None
pr_comments:
It looks like your PR touches production code but doesn't add or edit any test code. Did you consider adding tests to your PR?

IMO this should have a regression test. the following simple logic tests could be added:
```

```

finally, once it's fully fixed this should be backported.

```
panic: expected *DInt, found *tree.DBitArray

````

@rafiss  -- yeah, pretty trivial, but how do you explain https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/7fe93d78f572799da9a6c428768845962ceab610/pkg/ccl/changefeedccl/alter_changefeed_stmt.go#L87-L87?
One would assume (apparently incorrectly) that after type checking that argument is a Int, you should be able to call MustBeDint?
I guess the "idempotent part" makes sense.. But i think the API that takes a 3rd argument -- desired type, perhaps should not succeed if desired types don't match.  I don't know.

> But i think the API that takes a 3rd argument -- desired type, perhaps should not succeed if desired types don't match.

You are looking for `TypeCheckAndRequire` .

The contract of `TypeCheck` is that the `desired` type is just a hint: https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/618c73ae0893bf6d5a36097e76b9b5ddd847f6f4/pkg/sql/sem/tree/expr.go#L37-L49

Should all SQL plan hook execution be wrapped in a `recover()` so that these bugs can't crash the node? PlanHookFunction and PlanHookTypeCheckFunction take tree.Statement as arguments, so they're vulnerable to unexpected input the same as regular query execution.
reopening as per comment on https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/pull/108553/#issuecomment-1675026006 - this can still crash
@rafiss thanks for pointing out the problem of `alter changefeed (select 1) ...`.

review_comments:
i don't know the full history of why `alterChangefeedStmt.Jobs` is an expression, but looking a bit closer, i'm not sure this will work either. For example: `alter changefeed (select 1) add b;` also crashes the node.

what we'd need here is to evaluate the `alterChangefeedStmt.Jobs` expression. or else change `alterChangefeedStmt.Jobs` so it is not an expression.
